Section 1. Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) 
 
Saudi Water Partnership Company S.M.L.L.C established pursuant to the Supreme Economic 
Council’s resolution number 5/23 dated 23/03/1423, is owned 100% by the Ministry of Finance. 
Vision 2030 recognizes the critical importance of ensuring the future reliable provision of water 
supplies and sanitation services for the well-being and quality of life for all citizens of the Kingdom 
of Saudi Arabia ("KSA"). MEWA is responsible for achieving the water, agricultural and 
environmental related targets of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. 
 
Pursuant to a KSA Royal Court (40) Royal Order issued on 15/1/1440H (corresponding to 25 
September 2018), MEWA was given the right to procure a number of projects with private sector 
participation. MEWA has delegated its right to be procurer for the water projects to . 
 
The role for includes the following: 
 
• To be the off taker for all future Independent Water Projects (“IWPs”), Independent Water and 
Power Projects (“IWPPs”), Independent Sewage Treatment Projects (“ISTPs”) and Independent 
Strategic Water Reservoirs (“ISWR”). 
• To manage and lead the procurement process (in coordination with all stakeholders) for such 
independent projects from project initiation till negotiations, contract signing with developers, 
and oversight over construction; and, 
 
• To be fully involved in the downstream water sector, including activities like demand 
forecasting & management, selling of water and related power services to water 
authorities/independent bulk off-takers/ transmission companies and potentially management 
of subsidy payments and balance of accounts for the water sector. 
 
 
Section2. Purpose of the Project 
 
The Saudi Water Partnership Company (SWPC) is issuing this (RFP) to solicit proposals from 
qualified, Saudi Accreditation Center (SAAC)–accredited third-party laboratories for the provision 
of independent quarterly laboratory and validation services. These services will cover water, 
wastewater, and treated sewage effluent (TSE) samples collected from various ISTPs, IWPs, and 
IWPPs operating under SWPC’s portfolio across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. 
 
This engagement is intended to provide independent validation of plant performance, ensuring that 
the operational outputs of the facilities are in full compliance with contractual obligations and 
regulatory Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). The initiative forms part of SWPC’s ongoing 
commitment to operational transparency, quality assurance, and environmental compliance across 
its water and wastewater treatment infrastructure. 
 
Section3. Scope of Work 
While comprehensive requirements and technical specifications are outlined in the subsequent

sections of this document, the selected third-party laboratory will be responsible for performing the 
following key tasks: 
 
• Sampling and Analysis: Conduct sampling and laboratory analysis of potable water, 
wastewater, and TSE from designated ISTPs, IWPs, and IWPPs of SWPC asset portfolio 
located throughout the Kingdom. 
• Compliance with International Standards: Ensure that all sampling procedures, sample 
preservation, transport logistics, and laboratory analysis are carried out in accordance with 
recognized international standards 
• Reporting and Documentation: Submit comprehensive test reports within the mutually 
agreed timeline, which shall include the following: 
o Certificates of Analysis (CoA) 
o Chain-of-custody documentation for all samples collected 
o Comparative performance assessments against applicable contractual and regulatory KPIs. 
Plants Coverage 
As part of this assignment, the selected third-party laboratory will be required to conduct sampling 
and analysis at multiple plants currently operated under SWPC’s Public-Private Partnership (PPP) 
portfolio. These facilities are strategically located across various regions of the Kingdom of Saudi 
Arabia and vary in terms of design capacity, treatment technology, and applications. 
 
A detailed list of these plants, including their geographical location, and design capacity is provided 
below in Table-1. The selected third-party laboratory is expected to familiarize itself with the 
characteristics and operational contexts of each plant to plan and execute accurate and representative 
sampling and analysis.

Sampling and Analysis 
Frequency of Sampling and  
The third-party laboratory shall adhere to a clearly defined sampling and schedule to ensure 
consistent and timely monitoring of plant performance across all designated facilities. Sampling and 
laboratory shall be conducted on a quarterly basis, meaning once every three months, for each site 
listed under this scope. These quarterly sampling events will include the collection and analysis of 
sea water, potable water, wastewater, and treated sewage effluent (TSE) samples, as applicable, in 
alignment with the specific parameters and performance indicators detailed in the subsequent 
sections.

All sampling activities must be conducted in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) 
and internationally recognized protocols, ensuring sample representativeness, consistency, and 
reliability. The laboratory shall coordinate with each plant’s operations team to identify precise 
sampling points and confirm accessibility and safety requirements prior to sample collection. 
 
Quality Parameters to be Tested 
The third-party laboratory shall be responsible for the comprehensive analysis of water, wastewater, 
treated sewage effluent (TSE) and other by-products samples against a defined set of 
physicochemical, biological, and microbiological parameters. These parameters are aligned with the 
contractual Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and regulatory discharge/reuse standards. 
 
A detailed matrix outlining the full list of parameters is provided in the tables below. The laboratory 
is expected to perform all analyses in accordance with relevant standards (e.g., APHA, USEPA, 
ISO), accredited methods, ensuring precision, repeatability, and defensibility of results. 
 
All test results shall be reported with the appropriate units of measurement, detection limits, and 
benchmark values (as defined by the project agreements and regulatory frameworks). In addition, 
the laboratory shall flag any instances of non-compliance or abnormal values, along with expert 
commentary where applicable.

Reporting Requirements 
The third-party laboratory shall be responsible for preparing and submitting comprehensive, 
accurate, and timely analytical reports following each quarterly sampling and cycle. The reports 
must clearly present the test results, accompanied by appropriate interpretations, comparisons with 
applicable contractual Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and regulatory standards, and the 
identification of any non-compliances or anomalies.  
 
The report must also highlight any deviations, trends, or patterns observed in comparison to previous 
sampling rounds, providing SWPC with insights into performance stability or deterioration. 
 
Each report shall, at a minimum, include the following components as applicable for the respective 
period: 
 
• 
Executive Summary highlighting key findings, exceedances, or performance concerns 
• 
Detailed Results Table including sample ID, location, date/time of sampling, parameter name, 
measured value, unit, detection limit, reference standard/method, and relevant benchmark/KPI etc. 
• 
Chain-of-Custody Documentation showing traceability from sampling to reporting. The 
documentation must detail the sequence of sample handling—from initial collection, labeling, 
storage, and transportation, to final receipt and analysis at laboratory. It must include names, 
signatures, and timestamps of each person involved in the custody chain. 
• 
Certificates of Analysis (CoA) for all laboratory-tested parameters including verified results,  
methods, analytical technique used, laboratory accreditation details, and sign-off by an authorized 
laboratory official.  
• 
Laboratory Audit Results reflecting in-house sampling, preparation, and analysis practices and 
summarizing gaps or inconsistencies in test protocols or data management practices etc. 
• 
Photographic evidence of sampling activities and instrument calibration.  
• 
Comments and Recommendations by qualified analysts or lab experts with insight into the 
implications of the test results and conducted audits, potential causes of anomalies, patterns or
